Both halves resolved 2026-08-23; exoplasim/notes/physics-filter-stability.md carries the evidence.

THE BIAS HALF IS REFUTED, by the arm built to test it. The claim was that denergy26 carries the filter to the first power and denergy27 carries it squared, so 26-27 could not vanish under a nontrivial filter however well the core conserves. With the filter OFF, f = 1, both terms carry the same weight by construction and the bias term is exactly zero -- and the residual is the LARGEST of the whole grid, 0.5575 against 0.1204 for kappa 8 at the same step. Removing the bias raises the residual 4.6x where the hypothesis needs it to fall to zero. Confirmed across nine further cells: the residual grows monotonically as the filter weakens at every timestep.

What the dependences say instead is truncation error. It scales with the timestep, ratios of 0.60 at dt 30 and 0.38-0.41 at dt 22.5 against linear's 0.667 and 0.500, consistent across kappa 8, 4 and 2. So water-and-energy-closure.md's attribution to the semi-implicit step stands, and its number is not a constant of the model: 0.31 W/m2 is what this timestep and this filter cost. Eight-orbit arms confirm the short windows to within 2%.

THE UNBOOKED HALF IS BOUNDED, by an identity that runs the wrong way for it. Nothing books the filter's KE removal -- mkdheat covers Rayleigh friction and biharmonic diffusion, fluxmod the surface and vertical-diffusion terms, neither knows the filter exists -- and the filter preserves n=0 exactly so only the quadratic quantity is exposed. The kinetic-energy steady-state identity is what would find it, and a stronger filter removes more, so the gap must WIDEN with kappa if the filter is the missing term. It NARROWS: -0.013 to -0.000 at kappa 8, rising through +0.007 at kappa 2 to +0.039 with the filter OFF, where the filter's dissipation is identically zero and there is nothing to book.

At the adopted kappa 8 the identity closes to within 0.013 W/m2 against a conversion of about 2.1, six tenths of a percent. The term is real in principle and below what this instrument can see at production settings, so the row closes on the bound rather than on an mkdheat implementation.

REOPEN IF: the identity stops closing at the adopted kappa, or a rung's KE conversion grows enough that six tenths of a percent is worth chasing.

Settled 2026-08-23. The provenance finding stood and its conclusion did not: gp|exp|sp did come from the tidally-locked presets while the 45-minute step came from Earthlike, and the setting is load-bearing rather than inherited cargo. exoplasim/notes/physics-filter-stability.md has the arms, exoplasim/notes/parameter-decisions.md the argument.

THE FILTER BUYS TIMESTEP, so a filter strength and a timestep are one decision. Without the filter the model traps in the shortwave on the first radiation call at 45 minutes and runs at 22.5, and the requirement STRENGTHENS up the ladder: unfiltered, T42 runs at dt 30 and T170 needs dt 10. That is upstream's stated reason for filtering, measured rather than quoted -- a finer grid resolves sharper gradients off the same orography while a scale-free filter keeps cutting the same fraction.

KAPPA 8 AT EVERY RUNG, and it is not a compromise because it wins on both axes. Against kappa 4, 2, 1 and off it takes the longest stable step at every rung tested AND gives the smallest adiabatic non-conservation -- 0.3147 W/m2 at dt 45 against 0.3460, 0.4020, 0.6574 and a trap. What it costs is spectrum, which is the only reason not to go stronger: f is scale-free in n/NTRU with its half-power point at 0.737, so a stronger filter takes more of every rung's spectrum for a benefit nothing has measured. Nothing above kappa 8 was tested.

THE STEP IS THE PER-RUNG PART, and config/planet.yaml now carries it as model.resolution_timestep_minutes with check_consistency.py refusing a timestep_minutes that disagrees -- verified by making it disagree. T42 at 60 would be a third off every T42 run and is not adopted, because the roadmap's timestep experiment -- cold-start stability with traps armed, warm-start closure, climatological differences after settling, wall time per orbit -- has not been run. The projection removes 10.3 percent of zvgpg's norm, so rcsq = 1/cos^2 does carry it above NTRU and the truncation is not a no-op -- but the sink moves 2.2 percent and slightly the wrong way: denergy26-denergy27 goes -0.7938 to -0.8115 and Cimp-Ct -0.9588 to -0.9663, against a threshold of a third to pass and a tenth to refute, fixed before the arms ran. HS75's aliasing remedy does not touch this sink, which is consistent with world-pkf: the carrier is the damping removing divergence the conversion is charged half of, an operator-pairing effect and not an aliasing one. THE QUADRATURE now integrates in SURVIVAL space over the active region: with
S = exp(-(u/c)^k) the subgrid integral is integral_0^{S_t} flux(u(S)) dS, a
finite integral whose whole domain emits, so every point lands above the
threshold and the rule reaches arbitrarily far up the tail as S approaches zero.
Checked against a 20-million-point reference of the same integral:

    active fraction   old error   new error
       15.4 %          -10.2 %     -2.3 %
        0.76%          -65.0 %     -1.4 %
        0.011%        -100.0 %     -0.97%
        ~0             -100.0 %     -0.60%

The old rule was not merely blind in the tail; it biased EVERY arm low, and
returned exactly zero once the active fraction fell below about 0.01 percent.

MARTICORENA ET AL. (1997) IS WHY THEY DIFFER, and it says so directly: Saharan
lakes fed by streams "loaded with detritic sediments became clayey plains with
SMOOTH SURFACES", while "paleolakes, fed by superficial gypseous water, became
EMBOSSED TOPOGRAPHY, sensitive to weathering", with sebkha surfaces varying
"depending on their salt content and on the experienced periods of drying and
moistening". A clastic playa and an evaporite pan are a smooth surface and a
rough, more variable one.

MACKINNON ET AL. (2004) MEASURED THE ROUGH ONE. Their site 208 is a playa
carrying `saltpush` -- "salt push-ups or ridges created by expanding salt and
clay crusts on playa surfaces", 2 cm high, 5 cm apart -- and it is the strongest
sheltering species there, threshold friction velocity ratio 0.75 against 0.98
and 0.99 for the bushes beside it. Its aerodynamically derived z0 is 0.014 cm
over a 0.0053 to 0.039 cm range. That is the evaporite central value and bracket
unchanged.

PRIGENT ET AL. (2005) CARRIES THE SMOOTH ONE. The Bodele and Chott Djerid
depressions, the Sahara's strongest dust sources, "could have been lakes during
former wet climate periods, allowing accumulation of sediments. For those
regions it can be expected that the surface is relatively smooth, with low
roughness parameters." Their convention for active dust sources is 0.001 cm and
their sand-desert boundary is 0.02 cm, which set the ends.

CELLS COMBINE THEM as an erodible-area-weighted GEOMETRIC mean, because the drag
goes as 1/ln(z/z0) and it is ln(z0) that averages. The arms are now fields, not
scalars, so a cell of pure playa and a cell of pure evaporite sit at different
roughnesses within one arm.

REBUILT:

    central      10838.66       0.4133      3.020e-5
    high          2418.14       0.0922      1.006e-4

AND THE CROSSING IS NOW MARGINAL RATHER THAN TOTAL. It used to span "dust is
absent" to "dust dominates"; it now spans 0.0922 to 0.9701, and the only arm
below the threshold misses it by eight percent. The honest reading is that dust
DOES matter radiatively on this world and the open question is how much, not
whether. That is a statement about Vesper -- it carries far more closed-basin
playa than Earth does, at 17.49% of land erodible, and clastic playa is the
smooth end of the roughness range -- rather than about a missing measurement.

THE CENTRAL ESTIMATE MOVED UP 4.4x, from 0.0938 to 0.4133 AOD, and that is the
sourcing rather than a bug: the dominant erodible class is playa_clastic at
weight 1.0, and 3.0e-5 m is 3.3 times smoother than the generic 1.0e-4 m scalar
it replaced. A land-mean dust AOD of 0.41 is Saharan-everywhere and 10838 Tg/yr
is four to ten times Earth's total emission. Both follow from this world having
more playa, and both are worth a second opinion before anything downstream
treats them as settled -- but they are now what the sourced parameters give

Verdict 2026-08-24: DO NOT INHERIT. Holden et al. (2016) states what scf is for -- the frictional-geostrophic ocean dissipates wind energy, so increased surface wind strengths are required to compensate and drive a reasonable circulation. Conventional ensemble range 1 to 3, widened to 2 to 4 for the T21 coupling in anticipation of understated Southern Ocean zonal wind stress, and varied as one of six subjectively tuned ocean parameters over a 50-member ensemble. So it is not a regridding artifact and not derivable from the ratio of two stress products over a common grid: it is a class-16 knob, and the README's 2.0 and 2.6 are two settings of it. If GOLDSTEIN is adopted, scf is DECLARED as a bracket and the bracket is reported -- that requirement moves to OCN-3. The row's other half is also resolved: the offline regrid path this row tracks belongs to the EMBM architecture, which section 59b eliminates, so there is no path to reuse and the dependency on OCN-3 was dropped as moot. notes/external-model-survey.md sections 59b and 59e.
